title: Phase kickback: the target stays minus
objectives: Derive the phase-oracle action from an XOR oracle.
Explain global versus relative signs and the role of a final mixer.
prerequisites: Chapters 3–6: tensor products, unitary gates, joint-state order, coherent control and measurement.

quizzes.question: Why is minus a useful target for phase kickback?
options: X maps it to itself with eigenvalue −1.
It copies f into two unknown states.
feedback: Correct: the conditional eigenvalue becomes a branch-dependent sign.
The readout depends on the input and later circuit.
This is controlled phase accumulation, not cloning.

quizzes.question: For one-input f with f(0)≠f(1), what happens to a plus input with minus target?
options: The input becomes globally equivalent to minus.
feedback: Correct: the two input components gain opposite signs.
The target stays minus and factors out.
